dedupe_keys.name: usace locks and lock characteristics navigation data center lpms

description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Navigation Data Center produces and stores data on lock characteristics nationwide in the Lock Performance Monitoring System (LPMS) and the Lock Characteristics database, from surveys by its staff. The data cover the physical aspects of all locks the Corps built, maintains, owns or operates, grouped as location, physical characteristics, site information, site characteristics, management information and historical changes. The public Locks feature service held 234 lock chambers on 26 September 2026, with fields such as river and river mile, lift, chamber length and width, upper and lower sill depths, year opened, gate type, approach channel dimensions, mooring, district, owner and operator. LPMS itself is a web system that collects data on vessels passing through Corps locks in near real time. Coverage is national for the inland and coastal waterways. The data are free without use restrictions as an ArcGIS feature service; the NDC website at ndc.ops.usace.army.mil returned 403 to the cloud reader, so lock traffic reports were not read. Caveats: the data were made for national-scale use, and lock traffic and delay statistics sit in separate LPMS reports. The data support capacity planning, network flow and cascading failure studies of inland navigation. They complement the USACE National Waterway Network catalogued here.
